english: Basium's maul is a block of Carcerem bound within rune-inscribed Living Ivory. Living Ivory is a divine metal that heals and repairs itself, as well as helping its bearers heal faster. Carcerem is a crystal that captures and stores souls through Dimensional magic. The Fifth Law of The Compact strictly forbids using this to prevent a soul of any son of Nemed from passing freely into the vault of his god. The runes Basium inscribed on his maul shields mortal souls from being absorbed, but leave both Angels and Demons vunerable. This does not break The Compact as flagrantly as did the Sawol Cavea dagger, which Sabathiel had destroyed, should still be forbidden as once-mortal souls may still be captured after being processed in the heavens or the hells. A summoner of sufficient talent could release myriad demons from the Angelorum Cavea to do her bidding. [PARAGRAPH:4]Basium and the Boiling Sea[PARAGRAPH:2]At the end of the Age of Rebirth, the demon plagued lands of the Fane of Lessers were conquered and the Throne of Hell destroyed. Not content to just cleanse creation, the archangel Basium lead his angelic army into hell to continue his war. [PARAGRAPH]Decades passed and in that time the Bannor used the Crucible to weaken the world's magic. Powerful artifacts of past ages became dusty relics, and those with the talent to be mages in prior ages were rarely able to manifest their power. The Age of Invention had started. [PARAGRAPH]During this age three new goddesses appeared on creation, they were known as the Matronae. Morrigan was the goddess of fate and a great white temple was built to her on the cliffs of the Elohim city of Niveus. From Niveus came the gas Effluvium, which powered city lamp posts and caused divine visions (and would also be used by the Kuriotates to build airships). Sarabride was the goddess of vengeance and her temple was a great foundry built in the reclaimed city of Braduk the Burning. From her city came all sorts of wonders including coal powered trains. The citizens of Braduk built rail systems to connect the major cities of men. The last was Cliodna, the goddess of dreams, and her temple was built on the docks of the Bay of Laurus. From her temple came great steam powered ships that opened up travel to the distant shores of creation. [PARAGRAPH]All three goddesses were active in creation and their religions grew quickly. The religions of ages past, of distant gods who might answer occasional prayers were forgotten, or destroyed by the followers of the Matronae. What use is myth when gods walk among us?[PARAGRAPH]While this was happening Basium's angelic army battled through hell. They fought their way down the frozen slopes of the Throne of Hell, they waged war with frost giants, aquilan and the nive. They pushed through the draining swamps at the mountain's base and past the demonic locusts and the strange things that live beneath those dark pools. They laid siege to the iron city of Dis. Eventually they broke through the walls and Basium called to the citizens. [PARAGRAPH]"You are born of the gods. Do not sacrifice this for trivial rewards. Your immortal soul is worth more than safety, pleasure or power. "[PARAGRAPH]And though most cowered before the archangel, some cast aside their fear and joined him. [PARAGRAPH]Then Basium destroyed the Balor's that guarded the gate at the heart of the iron city. He trapped their souls in his great maul and walked through into the Bloodfield, and his army followed. [PARAGRAPH]Basium's army fought for years in the Bloodfield. And though they were tempted, none of them betrayed him. Yet one by one they died, torn apart by the Tormentors, the Umbral Horrors, the Pit Beasts and the Hell Wyrms. And this was Agares's plan. To draw Basium into hell, where no god could help him. Where he would be beaten, trapped and corrupted. [PARAGRAPH]Eventually Basium stood alone against the demonic hordes of the Bloodfield, countless demons trapped within his maul, his arms straining with the weight of it. It was then that the unholy god Camulos appeared. [PARAGRAPH]Camulos was a mountain of flesh, a creature with parts of a gorilla, snake and vulture. He had a hundred arms and screaming mouths scattered over his giant body. Their locations constantly changed as his flesh twisted, split and reformed. Hundreds of eyes covered him, those of animals and others never seen in creation. Barbed chains wrapped around his body and cut deeply into his skin, causing rivers of blood to pour from him and leaving his skin slick and red as if the spilled blood from every battle on Erebus flowed through him. As hideous as the demonic hordes were, they were nothing but dim reflections of the madness of the dark god of rage and war. [PARAGRAPH]All of Camulos's mouths roared and his roars were echoed by demons across the Bloodfield. He towered over the archangel, and without warning Camulos attacked. [PARAGRAPH]Basium could do little against the fury of a god. Basium was grabbed and pulled, beaten and slammed into the ground. Camulous beat him until Basium's chest collapsed, until his arms broke and his hips were crushed. All while a growing swarm of demons howled in triumph, and bit and tore at the battered archangel. [PARAGRAPH]Until a ring of golden fire sprung up around the broken Basium. Fire so hot it burnt demonic flesh. And even Camulous paused in his attack. [PARAGRAPH]A great rumble was heard across the Bloodfield. The ground shook and everything stopped. A great wave, so large that it dwarfed even the mountainous god, rolled across the Bloodfield, and it crashed down on them. Demons were scattered like dried leaves before the storm, many falling into the pits and ravines of the Bloodfield. Only Basium was unaffected as the golden fire turned all the water that struck it to steam. Camulous was knocked back, shocked and surprised as three masked goddesses flew overhead. [PARAGRAPH]Cliodna summoned up the water again and a dozen long tendrils of water stretched out from her, each with a dragon like face on the end. Together they bit and tore apart any demons that came close. Sarabride floated over the Bloodfield, glowing like a new sun, and cast down javelins of golden fire that destroyed demons and caused the new sea to boil. [PARAGRAPH]Morrigan landed over the broken Basium. She glared up at the raging god of war. [PARAGRAPH]"Come at me. " Morrigan said. "And I will show you that even gods die. "[PARAGRAPH]Camulous charged and Morrigan raised her hand, a stone so black it looked like a hole in creation was set in her palm. Out of it came a beam that consumed all it touched. Even the air of hell was destroyed by the beam. As the air was consumed more air rushed in and was destroyed as well, creating a screeching that grew louder as ebon tendrils and arcs twisted out from the beam. [PARAGRAPH]The beam struck the shoulder of the charging god. Any part the beam touched was simply gone. Not rotted, not burnt, not stabbed but unmade as simply as a candle being put out. [PARAGRAPH]And Camulous fled. [PARAGRAPH]As shocked as the demons were by the mountain sized tidal wave and the appearance of the three goddesses. The sight of Camulous running from battle shocked them even more. Across the Bloodfield demons crawling out of the flooded pits or even those on fire stopped to watch as Camulous disappeared. [PARAGRAPH]Sarabride and Cliodna landed by where Morrigan stood over Basium. [PARAGRAPH]"We have to go. " Cliodna warned. [PARAGRAPH]"We could go deeper. " Sarabride said. But the comment only received disapproving glances from the other two. [PARAGRAPH]Morrigan reached down to pick up Basium. [PARAGRAPH]"Who are you?" Basium asked, though his crushed chest made the words difficult. [PARAGRAPH]"Calm yourself my brother. " Morrigan whispered. "I have you. "[PARAGRAPH]And together the goddesses flew up and out of hell with Basium in their arms. [PARAGRAPH:3]Epilogue[PARAGRAPH]Gosea the Dwindling wandered through the wastes of hell. Once a withdrawn and abused girl in a Sheamic asylum, the voices had drawn her out. They had been the first ones to talk to her, to comfort her and to possess her. They transformed her from a quiet, terrified girl to a fearless summoner and mage. Until a battle on the streets of Bourne the Gleaming forced her to sacrifice those voices, to become once again timid and afraid. To be captured and executed for her crimes. [PARAGRAPH]Which brought her here, to the endless torments of hell. To be hunted and tortured until all mercy was lost, not that Gosea had much to give. [PARAGRAPH]Until a battle waged on the Bloodfield unlike any the eternal battleground had ever seen. In the wake of that battle the Bloodfield was eerily calm. Water still filled the fissures, the sun that briefly lit up the world was gone, blackened earth and burnt demonic corpses lay scattered about. The blood soaked ground showed where Camulos once stood. [PARAGRAPH]It was almost perfectly quiet. Almost. [PARAGRAPH]Gosea could hear whispering voices, so faint she thought it might just be the memories of the voices from the asylum. [PARAGRAPH]Following them lead her slowly through the battlefield. Past the remains of Basium's angelic army, past a shattered gore fiend, to a place where a perfect circle was burnt in the ground. [PARAGRAPH]But the voices weren't from the circle, but a short way off. From a small dip between the rough terrain that was still filled with water. [PARAGRAPH]Gosea waded into the pool. It was dark and muddy with the overturned earth. The water came nearly to her waist and she reached in, feeling rocks and the slick corpses of destroyed demons. But she reached beneath and felt something cool and hard, and in the instant she touched it, the voices flooded her mind with strength, purpose and power. [PARAGRAPH]She lifted the Angelorum Cavea, the great maul of Basium, out of the pool. She could feel the tens of thousands of demons trapped within the weapon. Centuries of demons defeated by Basium. Creatures from the Godswar, armies defeated right here in hell, all held within the rune inscribed weapon. And all available for her to channel.

[ICON_BULLET]The Maul wielded by [LINK=literal]Basium[\\LINK] is more than an instrument for slaying [LINK=PROMOTION_DEMON]Demons[\\LINK]; it is a cage for Demonic (or [LINK=PROMOTION_ANGEL]Angelic[\\LINK]) souls, preventing them from returning to trouble Erebus again. So long as this weapon exists, anyone seeking to [LINK=SPELL_RESURRECTION_GRAVEYARD]Resurrect[\\LINK] anyone it has slain must be holding the Angelorum Caveam. [LINK=SPELL_DESTROY_ANGELORUM_CAVEA]Destroying[\\LINK] it upon a [LINK=BUILDING_TEMPLE_OF_THE_VEIL]Demons' Altar[\\LINK] can bring all of the prisoners back.
The Heartstone

Anesidora is the only human soul who isn't descended from Nemed. She was given an immortal soul but without a true divine birthright the ages have worn heavily on her. Though trapped in Arawn's realm since her death early in the Age of Dragons, her cold heart was secreted out of the afterworld in the Age of Rebirth and she now exists as a dark draconic shadow under the sway of her heart's possessor. Though she isn't evil, she is destructive and manifests such sorrow that most enemies fall into despair when confronted by her. [PARAGRAPH]The Heartstone was among the items taken from the Netherworld by The Once-Elves when they escaped from bondage under Laroth and set up their own kingdom in the rift between that world and the world of the living. It was stolen from them and brought into Erebus itself by Gosea the Dwindling. During her escape she passed through a small Illian village called Brigdarrow. Here she was stopped and had her possessions searched due to suspicions that she was involved in the disappearance of three local children, who had actually just stayed out late trying to rescue an injured dog and his elven master. These were the only survivors after she hired three tribes of goblin mercenaries to burn the town and murder everyone who might have witnessed what she was carrying. Led by the elf's map and Auric Ulvin's innate ability to navigate by mana, the children fled through the Whispering Woods and into the Vale of Shadows to take refuge in the Once-Elves' City of Barathrum. There they were captured and imprisoned along with Talia, an elven druidess and witch whom King Haerlond Gosam's chief advisor (Waldrun, a Necromancer secretly in the employ of Laroth) had framed for Gosea's crimes. [PARAGRAPH:3]Mikel Alaunus grew up in a brutal Sheaim orphanage Mikel before fleeing to Bourne the Gleaming. Through devotion and talent Mikel became a soldier and a knight of the Empyrean. His most notable accomplishment was in defeating Gosea the Dwindling. [PARAGRAPH]When the War of the Deadlands began, Mikel was enlisted. He was killed in that war, and raised as an Undead Knight. After the Black Tower fell, Mikel became a leader of Marrowstone, the city of the sentient dead. He recovered the Heartstone from the rubble of the Black Tower and had it set in his breastplate. [PARAGRAPH]During the Age of Invention his daughter, Anna Alaunus came to the Deadlands to purge it. She was saved from the ravages of the mindless dead by Mikel. Mikel argued that the Lilim, the sentient dead, have as much right to "life" as the living, while Anna argued that he dishonors the memory of her father. [PARAGRAPH]In the end, Mikel gave the Heartstone to his daughter and she used it to open the Well of Souls, ending the curse of the Deadlands. But no sooner had it opened, than the Gossamer Legion matched out of it, lead by Ethne the White. [PARAGRAPH]The Lilim were not destroyed when the well was opened, but they ceased growing as those who died in their realm were no longer raised as undead.

[TAB]We marched through the wasteland of Agares' hell. We marched through the razor glass plains of Naraka, past the black waters of the Wraithsea and crossed the Westen Wall, a mountain range so foreboding even the balors gave up rather than follow us across. [PARAGRAPH]In hell we don't age, we don't thirst or hunger. The children at the time of the fall are still young, the few elderly that remain are still old. There is no death here, only torment eternal and the promise of escape. [PARAGRAPH]Sabathiel was the only one who scouted alone, and his trips took him further and further from our lines. In the beginning he scouted for a few hours, but now he was frequently gone for days. Today it was three weeks since the last time we saw him. Hundreds have been disappearing from our camp and I am no longer willing to wait for his return. [PARAGRAPH]"Capria, I suspect they were taken into Duke Eligos' lands. " Thom reported. Though he appeared a seven year old boy Thom had, like all of us, spent the past century in hell. He barely remembered a time before the fall. And he was one of our best scouts. [PARAGRAPH]"Then we will search for them. " I said. "Get Revelin and Donal, tell them to meet us at the gate. "[PARAGRAPH]It wasn't a real gate, we had no time to build walls. But the only place the Bannor were allowed to enter and exit the camp, it was where those entering the camp were blessed and prayed over, to make sure they weren't possessed. Anyone who approached from a different direction was killed. Knowledge of the gate was the first test to prove you were a friend. [PARAGRAPH]Which made the missing Bannor more puzzling. Over the decades we had endured attacks from underground, from the sky, or simply out of the darkness. But to have this many simply disappear. Some while on guard, often whole families and clans. We have never had an attack like this. [PARAGRAPH]Donal looked like a wildman compared to the austere Bannor. His beard was full and untrimmed, his smile jovial and his arms thicker than my legs. We had replaced at least a dozen of his shields, they would be beaten past repair in battle. But still Donal survived. [PARAGRAPH]Revelin had become an accomplished archer, scout and was my most trusted advisor after Sabathiel. [PARAGRAPH]"Has Sabathiel returned?" Revelin asked. [PARAGRAPH]"I'm done waiting for him. " I answered. "This time we will need to save ourselves. "[PARAGRAPH]We received blessing and atonement from the gate wardens, and though Revelin had more faith in his bow than the gods, he accepted the warden's prayer. [PARAGRAPH]Then we were off across the wastes. The ground was rough, with strange cilia just beneath the surface that moved and tensed as we passed, causing the ground to shift unexpectedly. Thom led the way, his knife in his hand and far enough ahead that we could barely see him in the world's perpetual gloom. If he raised his hand, we stopped and crouched to the ground. When he moved we moved with him. He led us as we avoided packs of wandering Dybbuk and Zabulus haunts. [PARAGRAPH]We hid, crept and ran for hours before Thom signaled for us to stop and crept back to us. [PARAGRAPH]"There's what looks to be an empty lake ahead. " Thom said. "All mud and drowned corpses, but no water. In the center there is a ruined tower, maybe twelve stories tall. We are clear to move closer if you would like to see. "[PARAGRAPH]We circled the lake for hours, looking for some way to approach the tower without passing by the hundreds of bodies half submerged in the lake bed. We didn't find on, but we did find the trail of hundreds of people meeting at the lake's shore. We spread out to investigate the tracks. [PARAGRAPH]"I'm not seeing any signs of a struggle. " Donal said, obscuring as many of the tracks as he uncovered as he tamped around the site. [PARAGRAPH]"Me either. " Thom said. "I assume these are the Bannor, but they aren't running, they aren't huddled together, there aren't impressions of them falling or being drug across the ground. "[PARAGRAPH]"There are demon tracks too. " Revelin said. "Harpazein, I think. Maybe they picked the people up here and flew them to the tower. "[PARAGRAPH]"Sounds like we are going after them. " I said. "Take a few minutes to rest, then we will cross the lake. "[PARAGRAPH]We sat at the edge of the lake, counting the bloated corpses, looking for handholds in the tower base that we would have to scale and signs of harpazein or worse flying into or out of the tower. [PARAGRAPH]"Are you taking the Sawol Cavea into the tower?" Revelin asked. [PARAGRAPH]I considered. The dagger hung inside my vest, as it has since I found it. We retrieved it from a Caducus that Sabathiel defeated. The dagger had the power to imprison souls. I used it whenever one of the Bannor couldn't be healed, would suffer forever, or simply wouldn't go on. [PARAGRAPH]"Everyone I trust to hold it is here. " I said. It was one of the reasons I never left the camp with Sabathiel, we could lose any individual life, even my own. But the Sawol Cavea held over six thousand Bannor souls. Souls I would, one day, release on Erebus so they could have a chance at heaven. [PARAGRAPH]"Why does Sabathiel make you carry it?" Donal asked. [PARAGRAPH]"I don't know. " I said. "He refuses to touch it, but I asked him if I shouldn't use it, he always avoids the question. Maybe one of his orders keeps him from interfering, or maybe he doesn't know what should be done with it any more than we do. "[PARAGRAPH]"Do we really need Thom?" Revelin asked. [PARAGRAPH]"You are right. " I said. "Thom, you have already done your part guiding us here. Take the Sawol Cavea back to the camp. Don't let anyone know you have it until Sabathiel returns, then give it him, or whoever he appoints as the new leader. "[PARAGRAPH]But Thom withdrew from the dagger. [PARAGRAPH]"No, I'm not going back without you. " Thom said, his look of determination, and the darkness in his eyes was unnatural on his smooth, small face. [PARAGRAPH]I tried again but it was useless. [PARAGRAPH]"Fine, then let us be quick, and careful. " I said, starting into the lake bed. [PARAGRAPH]The corpses we passed stirred and rose, angered at the interruption. Most got barely past their knees before one or two of us was on them cutting and chopping them back into another temporary sleep. It was a disgusting, gruesome business. Swollen flesh, bodies thick with black water and thin blood. Trudging through knee deep mud and body parts as we inched toward the tower. [PARAGRAPH]But eventually we made the tower, a rocky climb nearly four stories to the tower entrance that was once at the surface of the lake. Thom was easily up the rough wall, and thankfully the jagged rock provided enough handholds that it wasn't difficult for Revelin or I. But Donal was not made for climbing. His thick fingers found little purchase in the rocks, and his boots even less. Eventually the three of us climbed to the top and lowered a rope to help Donal follow behind us. [PARAGRAPH]The tower itself looked like a parapet that had been ripped off of a magnificent palace and stabbed into the center of the empty lake. Crumbling remains of the palace walls still clung to the tower, though they were nearly worn off. All the edges were worn smooth by time. The tower was topped by an open belfry, though it was impossible to see if anything was in it from here. [PARAGRAPH]There was a slight earthen base around the tower, and a few stone steps leading up to open entranceway. [PARAGRAPH]There are no intentional guards or locks in Hell, there is no reason for them. There are no thieves or enemy armies here. If someone more powerful than you wants something, which was rare in the sullen darkness before the fall, they simply took it. If someone less powerful than you wanted something of yours, they weren't fool enough to try to take it, not matter how openly you left it. We were more likely to come across a harpazein delivering a message to Eligos than to find one guarding the tower. [PARAGRAPH]The foyer was vaulted and faded mosaics were barely visible in the canopy, a map of an ancient city dressed in black and gold. The city's streets were laid out in perfect symmetry, and a series of monuments on all the streets directed the attention to the cities center. But that part of the mosaic was missing. [PARAGRAPH]Thom pulled me back a stair that spiraled up to the next level and signaled for me to be quiet. We all held still, somewhere above us something shifted in the darkness. We recognized the distant screeches and flutters of the harpazein, the scratching of imps claws across stone, and something more musical and seductive. A whispered voice, too quiet to be able to tell the words, but alluring. [PARAGRAPH]"Can you boys control yourself if we find a morrigain?" I asked. [PARAGRAPH]"Maybe what's leading the people away from the camp. " Donal said. Then as if realizing he didn't answer my question he added, "No different than any other demon in my mind, cut her down and move on. "[PARAGRAPH]Thom and Revelin nodded their agreement. But just in case I took lead on the stairs up. Let her try to entrance them after I lop her head off. [PARAGRAPH]The towers second level was a single hallway with rooms on each side. At the end of the hall a staircase continued up. There was less light here, in the first level open windows had filtered enough light into the large room, but here the windows were only in the side rooms. A small amount of light trickled out of the side rooms into the hallway, but even our well adjusted eyes were having problems seeing anything in the hall. [PARAGRAPH]After checking the first room was empty, I crept into the first thin shaft of light and signaled for the others to follow. Thom was up with me so quickly and quietly that I nearly stabbed him. Revelin followed, also quietly, he had his bow drawn and ready should the morrigain show herself. Donal lagged behind, making sure he wouldn't give us away. [PARAGRAPH]I checked each room as we passed them. They looked to be old studies, I could see the marks in the walls where bookcases and shelves once hung. The rooms were clear, even without the dust that covered everything in this world. [PARAGRAPH]"Did someone clean these rooms?" I whispered to Thom. [PARAGRAPH]He shrugged, also confused to see the rooms empty, but clean. [PARAGRAPH]When I reached the stairs at the other end of the hall I saw her. She was descending like a queen coming down to a grand ball. I could almost hear the musicians playing, the quiet of the crowd, the focus of the room on her. Her skin was pale and smooth, slight freckles played across her face like constellations in the night sky. And her eyes made the night sky envious. She wore only jewelry, emeralds and amethysts bound by thin gold chains to her perfect form. Though she didn't speak I could hear her voice echoing through the hall, whispers of pleasure, temptation, desire. [PARAGRAPH]Revelin's bow fired and it flickered harmlessly through the morrigain and splintered off the wall behind her. I shook myself, she continued down the stairs, but I realized the trap. [PARAGRAPH]"It's an illusion. " I said turning. [PARAGRAPH]At that Duke Eligos fell out of the shadowed recesses of the ceiling. He was massive, easily as heavy as an ox and he landed directly on Donal, slamming him onto the ground and placing one thick fist over Donal's head. Eligos resembled an ox in more than his size, long flat horns jutted out both sides of his head, his skin was course and reddish-brown, his eyes large and empty. He appeared to be a mix between a musk ox and a deviant child, happy to have cornered an animal to torment. [PARAGRAPH]Donal struggled beneath the duke's weight, but he couldn't move. [PARAGRAPH]Revelin spung his aim around at the duke, but didn't fire. [PARAGRAPH]"You have stolen our people. " I said, inching closer to the Duke. [PARAGRAPH]"I've stolen nothing. " he said, where I expected to see the cold intelligence of a predator in his eyes I saw only juvenile glee. "They came to me willingly, they traded your war for the comforts of my home. "[PARAGRAPH]"Where are they?" I asked. [PARAGRAPH]"I was an angel once. " he said, avoiding my question. "A son of Amathaon, I created the first plum. You have never seen beauty like his gardens. And I lived with others. Now I live with others again. "[PARAGRAPH]"They are not your playthings. "[PARAGRAPH]Eligos snarled at me and put his weight on Donal's head, causing him to howl in pain. I stopped moving. [PARAGRAPH]"I saved them. " Eligos said. "They came to me, begged me to allow them to live in my tower. They are all here, we will create a new garden here. "[PARAGRAPH]"No one came to you. " I said. [PARAGRAPH]"Oh yes, one did. Then he went back to your camp and told them of my offer. And they came, hundreds of them came. "[PARAGRAPH]"Who?" I asked. [PARAGRAPH]The hallway was quiet, Eligos savored the tension, but he was not the one who broke it. [PARAGRAPH]"Capria. " Revelin began. "We have given a century to Sabathiel. How many more should we give? We are trapped in hell, why can't we make the best of our prison?"[PARAGRAPH]I blinked away tears of frustration and pain. When I spoke my voice was calm and emotionless. [PARAGRAPH]"You have been leading the people away from the camp, serving them up to demons?" I said. [PARAGRAPH]Donal's complaints were much more emphatic, "You rutting godless bite. "[PARAGRAPH]Donal struggled and nearly pushed Eligos off of his back. Revelin changed his aim from Eligos to Donal, for a second the demon seemed to be forgotten. Thom used that second to leap on Eligos, easily vaulting himself off the duke's think forearm and stabbing the duke in the chest with his knife. [PARAGRAPH]Eligos caught Thom in his free hand and smiled, the knife blade was half buried in the demon's chest, but it barely pierced his thick, rough skin. [PARAGRAPH]"A mere boy cannot kill me. " Eligos said. [PARAGRAPH]"I am not a mere boy. " Thom said, though he spoke with the voice of angels. [PARAGRAPH]The boy was gone. Sabathiel was held in the demon's hand instead, and the knife was Sabathiel's gleaming sword. Sabathiel shoved it through the demon's chest and Eligos crumbled into fractured pieces of flesh. Sabathiel pulled Donal out from underneath the disgusting pile while I turned on Revelin. [PARAGRAPH]"I'm sorry Capria. " Revelin said. "I am trying to save the Bannor too. I didn't believe Fanum when he said that we would be safe right on the other side of the mountain. There were only more demons there. And I don't believe that story now. We need to find a place where we will be safe, be reasonable. "[PARAGRAPH]"Fanatical opposition is the only reasonable response to the threat of hell. " I had parroted that line many times, sentenced many who would negotiate with demons to death. But none I cared for as much as Revelin. I drew the Sawol Cavea from beneath my breastplate. Sabathiel and Donal watched quietly. [PARAGRAPH]"You aren't the first to claim that. " Revelin begged. "Just leave me here. "[PARAGRAPH]"Though you are willing to doom your immortal soul, I am not. The effect of the Sawol Cavea was immediate, his features became gaunt and pained. His scream was choked short and his body fell to ash. The dagger felt as warm as fresh blood in my hand. [PARAGRAPH:3]Upon returning to Erebus, Capria personally performed a ceremony to destroy the Sawol Cavea. Sabathiel refused to touch the carcerem blade, as such use of dimensional magic to rob the gods of the souls they are owed violates the 5th Article of the Compact. After the conquest of the Fane, the Bannor would again turn to the use of such magic in order to build the prison of Judicium.

Once Belphegor is vanquished, Basium passes into the Infinite Garden. All the guardians and hosts of the Garden stand aside as the archangel walks to the center of the world, where the Font of Life rests in the Garden's cradle. Sucellus stands watch over the Font. Basium sets down his weapon and asks for Sucellus's permission to take the Font into Creation and resurrect Yggdrasil. Sucellus answers:[PARAGRAPH]"If I gave it, would you lay down power? The ability to resurrect the army that marched into hell with you and every enemy of the fallen? You, who broke the Compact, the laws of your dominion and god? You, the archangel of life that has killed more than any demon? You, who has refused to serve the god of your dominion? Would you return the Adamans Animans so easily?"[PARAGRAPH]Basium simply offers that he will and Sucellus allows him to take the Font of Life from the Infinite Garden and into Creation. Across Creation the effect can be felt as the health of all people, plants and animals improve. Plants bloom, pregnancies sweep all manner of life across creation (many immaculate) and the children born of these pregnancies are gifted with talent, health and life that hasn't been seen since the Age of Magic. [PARAGRAPH]The angel Gwenhwyfar approaches Basium after this miracle, begging him to use the Font to continue to strengthen creation. She warns that Ars Morendi, Buboes, Stephanoes and Yersinia still plague Creation and that the Font can be used to destroy them. [PARAGRAPH]Basium refuses, saying that he must return the Font. But Gwenhwyfar's phoenix lands on the archangel's arm. Basium speaks to the phoenix, then transforms him into the sword Apricus, also known as the Sword of Life, or Demonsbane. Apricus glows brightly and is so powerful lesser demons will be killed by the touch of its light alone. Basium places an arda on Apricus, that it may only be wielded by mortal hands. [PARAGRAPH]Basium leaves Apricus by Yggdrasil, for Gwenhwyfar to watch over (as an angel she can not wield it) and returns to the Infinite Garden where he places the Font of Life back in its cradle.

When trying to capture a mature city, bring plenty of siege weapons. You will want to bombard the defenses and to soften up the defenders. If you don't have siege available, fireball-casting mages make a good substitute. Treants and especially Earth Elementals work well too.

Be aware of the strengths and weaknesses of units. For example, Crossbowmen and Longbowmen get a bonus when defending cities, while assassins and marksmen can choose to attack the weakest combat unit in a stack. Phalanxes excel at conquering cites, while Berserkers cause collateral damage.

Consider keeping one unit with the Medic promotion in every large stack-the bonus isn't cumulative, but it can make the difference in keeping an advance going. Disciple class units are the only ones who begin with this promotion, apart from The Grigori Civilization's Grigori medic unique unit. Recon, Arcane, and Disciple units can purchase Medic 1 once you know the Medicine technology.

Watch for announcements about religions being founded and wonders being completed-this can give you a hint as to how advanced your foes are. Should you build the Eyes and Ears network wonder you will be able to see what your rivals research, so long as you are in the Undercouncil.

Some religions do not get along very well. The Order has trouble coexisting in the same city with The Undertow or The Ashen Veil. The Empyrean has trouble coexisting in the same city with the Council of Esus or The Ashen Veil. The Children of the One have trouble coexisting with any other religion.
Unlike in normal Fall from Heaven 2, there are no technologies that have state religion prerequisites in Magister Modmod for FfH2

Paladins are special units only available to Good nations and only nations with an Evil alignment can train Eidola. (Unlike in normal Fall from Heaven 2, Druids are not restricted to the Neutral Alignment as they are priests of the Unblemished. ) Alignment is displayed by score and modified by religion.

Mary Morbus, Yersinia, and Sects of the Flies can spread the plague. Sect of the Flies an Infernal unique unit than replaces Champions. Yersinia is a Barbarian hero. Mary Morbus may be given to a player who has built an Alchemy Lab. Units with Death Affinity and either Body Affinity or the Undead race may learn Plague Carrier in order to spread this illness too.

Immortals are reborn in the owner's capital after dying, with all their experience and promotions, but only once per turn. To kill Immortals forever you must kill them twice in a single turn, unless you use the Nether Blade, the Angelorum Cavea, an Angel of Death, or the Soul Shroud.

Units killed by werewolves might become werewolves too. Ravenous Werewolves are hard to control, but become more manageable as well as stronger once they have killed living units. A werewolf keeps the promotions it had before being infected with Lycanthropy, but is not able to cast spells. Assuage, the top level Spirit spell, is the only known cure for Lycanthropy.
The Hero promotion gives the unit 1 XP per turn until it reaches 500 XP. It also gives access to the Heroic Strength and Heroic Defense promotions, and makes the unit immune to becoming rebellious.

Some units can be trained only if you have the required state religion. You can't train Crusaders without the Order religion, and you can't train Satyrs without the Fellowship of the Leaves religion. Radiant Guards usually require The Empyrean and Nightwatches usually require the Council of Esus, but the Overcouncil and the Undercouncil can vote to waive these requirements for their members.

Civilizations with the Organized trait can build Command Posts even without Great Commanders. Other nations must use Great Commanders to construct them. Similarly, the Philosophical trait allows a player to build Academies without sacrificing Great Sages.

Heroes and Apocalypse units are World Units. Each World Unit can be created only once. If such a unit dies, it can not be recreated. It can however be resurrected using the Life 3 spell, which will bring the unit back with its promotions etc intact.
Mages' Fireballs cause collateral damage and can bombard city defenses. The duration of Fireballs will not be affected by the Summoner trait.

Blight will strike all players (except the Infernals) as the Armageddon Counter rises. It gives a large health penalty to every city and damages every unit. You can prepare for the penalty by building health-granting buildings, and not letting your cities grow too large until after it hits. Note that while Blight only hits once, the Pestilence event (which has a similar but smaller health penalty) can occur multiple times.

Never despair in the face of a large stack of units. A Mage's Fireball may not be strong, but it can do a lot of damage to an enemy stack. Other spells can deal damage directly to stacks of any size. A few spells, like Destroy Undead (Greater) or Snowfall (Greater), can even kill whole stacks of the right kinds of units. If you have no mages, use ranged units.
